transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well... I suppose occupational health sent me. I didn't really ask for the appointment, but they noticed a pattern and wanted me to come in. I just tend to push breakfast and lunch aside when I'm busy with lab runs or exhibition work. And... I guess by the time I actually eat, I just keep it to something very small and controlled. So, that's why I'm here.
Do you ever feel anxious about gaining weight or have concerns about your body shape or size?

I... I suppose so. It's just... if the scale goes up, even a fraction, I feel this... sharp panic. It just makes me feel like I'm losing the discipline I've worked so hard to maintain. I just prefer to keep things exact.
After eating, do you ever make yourself sick or exercise excessively to control your weight or shape?
No... I don't do that. I don't make myself sick. And I don't really exercise, either... I'm usually too busy at the lab for anything like that anyway. So, no.
When you think about your ideal weight or body shape, how do you picture it, and how important is it for you to reach that?

I... I don't really have an ideal number in mind. It's more about what I see. When I look in the mirror before leaving for work, I just... I don't see someone thin. I mostly just notice my stomach, or my hips... and it just makes me feel like I look... careless. Like I'm unserious about my work. It's just important to me to not look like that.
How often do you find yourself preoccupied with these thoughts about your body shape or weight, and does it interfere with your daily work or life at all?

I... I suppose it's on my mind a fair amount. But it doesn't stop my work. I'm still meeting all my main deadlines. I just... I don't really go to the lab lunches anymore. Or those informal planning meals we have. It's just easier to stay at my desk. I guess I'm a bit more isolated from my colleagues than I used to be... but the work gets done.
When you choose what to eat in a day, how much does your concern about your body shape or weight influence what or how much you eat?

I... well. I suppose that's actually why occupational health sent me here in the first place. 

I've just... gotten into this pattern. During my lab runs or exhibition work, I tend to just push breakfast and lunch aside. And then... by the time I finally do eat, I just make sure to keep it to something very small. Just... controlled. It's just easier that way.
When you choose to eat very little, is it mainly because of the way you feel about your body, or is it more about losing interest in food or not feeling hungry?

I... I suppose I do still get hungry. It's not really a lack of interest. 

It's... well, if I see the scale go up, even just a fraction, I... I get this sort of sharp panic. It just feels like I'm losing the discipline I've worked so hard to maintain. So... yes, I suppose it is mostly because of how I feel about my body. I just need to keep things under control.
When you look at yourself in the mirror, do you see yourself differently than others might, or do you feel like certain parts of your body appear larger than they actually are?

I... I don't know how others see me. But... when I look in the mirror before I leave for the lab, I... I definitely don't see someone thin. 

I just... my eyes always go straight to my stomach. Or my hips. And... it just makes me feel like I look careless. Like I'm not... serious about myself. I just... I don't like what I see.
Outside of avoiding meals with colleagues, has this pattern of eating or concern with your body affected other areas of your life, like your relationships, mood, or ability to focus on tasks?

I... my work is fine. I'm still meeting all the main deadlines. 

But... I suppose I have stopped going to the lab lunches. And the informal gallery planning meals. I just... avoid them now. So... I guess I am a bit more isolated from my colleagues than I used to be. But I get my work done.

When you look at yourself, do you feel that certain parts of your body, like your stomach or hips, appear larger than they actually are, or do you feel that how you see yourself matches what others would see?

I... I don't really know how to answer that. I just... I see what I see. I don't know if it matches what other people see. I just know that when I look at those areas, they... they look too big to me.
